title: Grandpa's Famous Pancakes
text:
Grandpa makes pancakes every Sunday. He says this recipe has been in our family for {number} years.

First, put two cups of flour in a big {adjective} bowl. Add one egg, a cup of milk, and a handful of {plural noun}. Stir it {adverb} with a wooden spoon until it looks smooth.

Next, pour the batter into the pan in the shape of a {noun}. Wait until the pancake starts {verb ending in ing}, then flip it. Grandpa has one rule: never {verb} near the stove. Last week one pancake {past tense verb} right off the plate and landed on the dog's {body part}.

Top each stack with syrup and three {plural noun}. Grandpa eats his in his big green chair and hums a song about {plural noun}.

Grandma says his pancakes taste like {food}. Grandpa says that is the most {adjective} thing anyone has ever told him.

title: Cooking with Chef Noodle
text:
Hello and welcome to Cooking with Chef Noodle! Today we are making the most {adjective} soup in the whole world.

First, I fill my big pot with water and {plural noun}. Then I add a carrot, some {plural noun}, and one small {noun}. My helper, Rosa, will {verb} the soup with this long spoon. Very nice, Rosa!

Now for my secret ingredient: a spoonful of {food}. My grandmother taught me that trick when I was {number} years old. She always said, "Never stir the soup with your {body part}."

Oh, look! The soup is {verb ending in ing} already. That means it is ready. Mmm! It tastes {adverb} wonderful, like a warm {noun} on a rainy day. Rosa {past tense verb} and asked for seconds.

Thank you for watching! Next week, Rosa and I will make a sandwich out of {plural noun}.

title: Today's Menu at the Wobbly Spoon
text:
Welcome to the Wobbly Spoon Cafe! Please sit at any table except the one with the {adjective} chair.

Soup of the day: Cream of {plural noun}. It is warm, thick, and only a little bit smelly.

Dessert: Chocolate cake with {color} frosting. Kids who finish it get to {verb} with Mr. Bean in the kitchen.

Please wait {adverb} for your food. If you {past tense verb} during your meal, please tell Mr. Bean.

title: Rules for Our Kitchen
text:
Mom wrote these rules on a card and stuck it to the fridge with a {adjective} magnet.

Rule one: Always wash your hands before you touch the {plural noun}.

Rule two: Please do not {verb} on the kitchen table. Use the back yard for that.

Rule three: If you open the fridge, close it {adverb}. The milk does not like to be surprised.

Rule four: The cookie jar is shaped like a {noun}. You may have one cookie after dinner, or {number} cookies on your birthday.

Rule five: Never put {plural noun} in the soup pot. Grandpa did that once, and the soup turned {color}.

Rule six: Whoever cooks does not wash the dishes. Last night Dad made {food}, so I washed every plate while {verb ending in ing}.

Rule seven: The dog may not sit at the table, even if he asks {adverb}.

Rule eight: Everyone must say "{exclamation}!" before we eat. Grandma {past tense verb} the first time she heard it.

title: The Night I Helped Make Tacos
text:
Dear Diary,

Tonight I helped Dad make tacos for the whole family. I wore my {adjective} apron and a tall chef hat. Dad said I looked like a real {noun}.

My job was to wash the lettuce and set out the plates. I also got to {verb} the beans, which was my favorite part. For a surprise topping, I picked {plural noun}.

When dinner was ready, I rang a little bell. My sister came running {adverb} into the kitchen. My baby brother {past tense verb} in his high chair. Even our cat sat by the table and stared at the {plural noun}.

Everyone said the tacos were {adjective}. Grandma ate {number} tacos and then asked for a bowl of {plural noun}. Grandpa said they tasted just like {food}.

Tomorrow I get to help with breakfast. Dad says I can crack the eggs if I promise not to {verb} while {verb ending in ing}.

Love,

title: Thank You for the Cookie Recipe
text:
Dear Grandma,

Thank you for sending me your secret cookie recipe. I made the cookies with Mom on Saturday, and they came out {adjective}.

We mixed the flour, sugar, and eggs in your old {color} bowl. Then we added two cups of chocolate chips and one cup of {plural noun}, just like you wrote. Mom said the dough smelled like a {noun}.

I rolled the dough into {number} little balls. We waited at the table while {verb ending in ing}. When the timer rang, the whole house smelled {adverb} sweet.

I gave one cookie to our neighbor, Mr. Park. He {past tense verb} and asked for the recipe. I told him it is a family secret, but it has a little bit of {food} in it.

Our dog, Pepper, tried to {verb} on the cookie tray, so Mom hid the last cookie in a {noun}.

Please come visit soon so we can bake {plural noun} together. Bring your {adjective} apron!

Love,
Sam

title: Breaking News from the Bake Sale
text:
Good evening. This is Kid News with breaking news from the bake sale at Pine Hill School.

This morning, the second graders set up a long table full of treats. There were brownies, banana bread, and a giant cake shaped like a {noun}. The line went all the way to {place}.

The most popular treat was a muffin made by Ava and her dad. Ava says the secret is a handful of {plural noun}, stirred in {adverb}. One teacher bought {number} muffins and {past tense verb} back to her classroom.

The cupcake table was also very {adjective}. Each cupcake had a tiny {noun} on top. Mr. Diaz, the gym teacher, ate one while {verb ending in ing}.

The bake sale raised enough money to buy new {plural noun} for the library. The principal said it was the most {adjective} day of the year.

Next month, the first graders will bake a cake so big that they can {verb} inside it. Back to you, Tom. Please save me a {food} muffin.

title: How to Set the Table
text:
Setting the table is an important job. Here is how my family does it.

Step one: Put a {adjective} placemat in front of every chair. Ours have pictures of {plural noun} on them.

Step two: Put a plate on each placemat. Make sure the plates are not upside down, or the food will {verb} right off.

Step three: Put the fork on the left and the spoon on the right. Next to the spoon, put a napkin folded into the shape of a {noun}.

Step four: Fill each cup with water, milk, or {food}. Carry the cups {adverb} so nothing spills.

Step five: Put a bowl of {plural noun} in the middle of the table. Grandma likes to add a {adjective} candle.

Step six: Give the dog his own tiny plate with a {noun} on it. He {past tense verb} the first time we did that.

When you are done, ring the dinner bell and shout "{exclamation}!" Everyone will come {verb ending in ing} into the room and ask for {plural noun}.

title: A Note in Your Lunchbox
text:
Good morning, sweetie!

There is a turkey sandwich in your lunchbox, cut into four little squares, the way you like it. I also packed some grapes, a cheese stick, and a small bag of {plural noun}. Please do not trade the cheese stick for a {noun} again.

For a treat, there is one cookie with {color} sprinkles. You may eat it {adverb} after you finish your sandwich.

Remember to wash your {body part} and drink your water. Ms. Fern says kids who drink water can {verb} much better in the afternoon. I also packed a {adjective} napkin and a spare {noun}, just in case.

After school, we are going to the park to see the {plural noun}. Then we will go home and make {food} for dinner together.

Have a {adjective} day! I am so proud of you for {verb ending in ing} so nicely in class this week. Ms. Fern says you {past tense verb} like a superstar.

Love you to the moon,

title: Our Secret Birthday Cake Plan
text:
Dad's birthday is on Saturday, and my sister and I are making him a surprise cake. Here is our plan.

Step one: Hide all the baking things in the {noun} so Dad does not find them.

Step two: Mom will take Dad to the store to buy new {plural noun}. While they are gone, Aunt June will help us bake. She makes the best {food} in town.

Step three: Make a chocolate cake with {adjective} frosting. Write "Happy Birthday" on top with tiny {plural noun}. My sister wants {number} candles, but Aunt June says that might be too many.

Step four: Hide the cake {adverb} under a big {noun}.

Step five: When Dad comes home, we will turn off the lights and {verb} behind the couch. Then we will jump out and yell "{exclamation}!" as {adverb} as we can.

Last year Dad {past tense verb} when he saw his cake. This year, we will sing to him while {verb ending in ing}.
